title: Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. Isabela Cultural Corporation
summary: The Supreme Court ruled on the proper timing of tax deductions for accrual-basis taxpayers. Under the all-events test, an expense is deductible in the taxable year in which all events have occurred that establish the fact of the liability and the amount can be determined with reasonable accuracy.
doctrine: Under the accrual method of accounting, an expense is deductible for the taxable year in which all the events have occurred that establish the fact of the liability and the amount thereof can be determined with reasonable accuracy (all-events test). The actual payment of the expense is not determinative.
fullText:
YNARES-SANTIAGO, J.:

The issue is the proper taxable year in which certain expenses may be claimed as deductions by a taxpayer using the accrual method of accounting.

Under the accrual method of accounting, income is reportable when all the events have occurred that fix the taxpayer's right to receive the income, and the amount can be determined with reasonable accuracy. Similarly, an expense is deductible when all events have occurred that establish the fact of the liability and the amount can be determined with reasonable accuracy.

This is known as the all-events test. Under this test, it is the right to receive income or the fact of the liability — not the actual receipt of income or payment of expense — that determines the taxable year.
